JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 11-06-2021 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on her motorcycle bearing No. KA-42-EC-4813, from Doddakabbali towards Yakkuli village, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, slowly and cautiously, on the extreme left side of the road.

When she was near Madeshwara Temple at Doddakabbali village,
Kodihalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagaraka District, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664 came in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Shubodaya Hospital, Kodihalli, wherein she took first aid treatment and then she was shifted to Kanakapura Government Hospital, wherein she took conservative treatment and then she was shifted to Jayanagara Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient and underwent surgery.

Earlier to the accident, she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work at Gramina Koota, Kodihalli and earning Rs.15,000/-
per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she became permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Kodihalli Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two-wheeler for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

2 3.
On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EA-8664 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664 in the alleged accident.
It has further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.
It has contended that the petitioner herself was solely responsible for the alleged accident and there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.

It has further contended that the petitioner and the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the petitioner was not wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 11-06-2021 at about 6.30 p.m.,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle, bearing registration No. KA-09-EA-8664?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.

What order or Award?
6.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr.
Prashanth N., as P.W.2 and closed her side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

3 REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 11-06-2021 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on her motorcycle bearing No. KA-42-EC-4813, from Doddakabbali towards Yakkuli village, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, slowly and cautiously, on the extreme left side of the road.

When she was near Madeshwara Temple at Doddakabbali village,
Kodihalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagaraka District, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EA-8664 came in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work at Gramina Koota, Kodihalli and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and whereby lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., and first information statement, Ex.P.2 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.3 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.4 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.5 is OPD book issued by Kanakapura Government Hospital, Ex.P.6 are OPD slips (total 5), Ex.P.7 are medical bills (total 4), Ex.P.8 is x-ray, Ex.P.9 is notarised copy of Aadhar card,
Ex.P.10 is notarised copy of driving licence, Ex.P.11 are four photos with memory card and Ex.P.12 are x-rays (total 2).

11. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of vehicles, injuries caused to petitioner in the accident, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company, though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not examined its official, to depose the contention taken in the written statement on oath.
The respondent has not adduced any evidence to establish the contentions taken in its written statement.
There is no evidence on record to show that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner herself or there is some contributory negligence on her part.

Further, the petitioner/ P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to her self rash and negligent driving and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664.

Further, she has clearly denied the suggestion that, the alleged accident has caused by some unknown vehicle and not by the motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664 and she has lodged false complaint against the driver of insured vehicle of the respondent No.1.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

4 12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 4, prima-facia it reveals that, on 11-06- 2021 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on her motorcycle bearing No. KA-42-EC-4813, from Doddakabbali towards Yakkuli village, slowly and cautiously, on the extreme left side of the road.

When she was near Madeshwara Temple at Doddakabbali village,
Kodihalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagaraka District, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EA-8664 came in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind.
Due to the impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EA-8664 the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of her body.

13. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.5 OPD book, Ex.P.6 OPD slips (total 5) and Ex.P8 and Ex.P12 x-rays (total 3), it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and she has suffered abrasion over left eye, abrasion left upper lip sutured wound in right chin 4cm x 2 cm x 1 cm, loss of front teeth, fracture of left condylar TMJ and avulsed upper four front teeth.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, on 05-07-2021, the petitioner was brought to Oral Care Orthodontic and Implant Clinic, Bengaluru, with the history of road traffic accident and on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner had suffered the injuries i.e., deviation of jaw,
unable to open the mouth, facial disfigurement, laceration on face mareon chin, avulsion of upper front teeth and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. prosthetic treatment to replace the lost teeth and intermaxilary fixation process.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EA-8664 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
14. Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.2, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and the accident has taken place on account of dashing the offending motorcycle to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and there was no negligence on the part of petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.4, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-EA-8664.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of Sowjanya vs Nishanth Vijaya Varsiya on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161046484/
5 offending motorcycle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 11-06-2021 at about 6.30 p.m.,
near Madeshwara Temple at Doddakabbali village, Kodihalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk,
Ramanagaraka District, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-09-EA-8664.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EA-8664 and she has sustained abrasion over left eye,
abrasion left upper lip sutured wound in right chin 4cm x 2 cm x 1 cm, loss of front teeth, fracture of left condylar TMJ and avulsed upper four front teeth and for the said injuries she has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card and driving licence, which are marked as Ex.P.9 and 10.
As per Ex.P.9 and 10, the date of birth of the petitioner is 27-09-1999.
The accident has taken place on 11-06-2021 at about 6.30 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 22 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief Sowjanya vs Nishanth Vijaya Varsiya on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161046484/
6 affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered deviation of jaw, unable to open the mouth, facial disfigurement, laceration on face mareon chin, avulsion of upper front teeth and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. prosthetic treatment to replace the lost teeth and intermaxilary fixation process.
Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 45% disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.5 OPD book, Ex.P.6 OPD slips (total 5) and Ex.P8 and Ex.P12 x-rays (total 3), clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered deviation of jaw, unable to open the mouth, facial disfigurement, laceration on face mareon chin, avulsion of upper front teeth and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. prosthetic treatment to replace the lost teeth and intermaxilary fixation process.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
The P.W.2 has deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, the petitioner has suffered disability of 45% due to injuries suffered in the accident.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has not assessed the physical disability of the petitioner.
Further he has admitted that, the lower teeth and jaws of the petitioner are not damaged and there is no dis-figuration or the mal-alignment in the lower jaws.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, now the petitioner can speak normally and drink the water and consume food.

It is pertinent to note that, no where in the evidence the P.W.2 has stated that,
the petitioner requires any further treatment in the future.
The petitioner has not produced any document to show that, due to accidental injuries she has suffered any physical disability.
The oral and documentary evidence on record clearly goes to show that, the petitioner has not suffered any physical disability and the injuries suffered by her are completely cured.
Further, the petitioner has failed to establish that, before accident she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to above injuries sustained in the accident she has suffered physical disability and she is not in a position to attend her day to day work.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of future income.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges etc.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 4 medical bills, as per Ex.P.7.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.1,51,407/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,51,407/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
abrasion over left eye, abrasion left upper lip sutured wound in right chin 4cm x 2 cm x 1 cm, loss of Sowjanya vs Nishanth Vijaya Varsiya on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161046484/
7 front teeth, fracture of left condylar TMJ and avulsed upper four front teeth.

As per Ex.P.5 OPD book issued by Kanakapura Government Hospital and Ex.P.6 OPD slips, the petitioner has taken treatment at Kanakapura Government Hospital and Oral Care Orthodontic and Implant Clinic,
Bengaluru.

Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner,
this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.5 OPD book issued by Kanakapura Government Hospital and Ex.P.6 OPD slips, the petitioner has taken treatment at Kanakapura Government Hospital and Oral Care Orthodontic and Implant Clinic, Bengaluru.

v) Food and nourishment:

The petitioner is the resident of Yakkuli, Doddaabbali, Kodihalli Hobali,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagar District, the accident has taken place near Madeshwara Temple at Doddakabbali village, Kodihalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagaraka District and she has taken treatment at Kanakapura Government Hospital and Oral Care Orthodontic and Implant Clinic,
Bengaluru.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work at Gramina Koota, Kodihalli and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do Field Executive Loan Collector work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

Therefore,
notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner has taken treatment at Kanakapura Government Hospital and Oral Care Orthodontic and Implant Clinic, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.

sentences.text: She might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,000 x 2 = Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.

8 viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 22 years and unfortunately she has suffered abrasion over left eye, abrasion left upper lip sutured wound in right chin 4 cm x 2 cm x 1 cm, loss of front teeth,
fracture of left condylar TMJ and avulsed upper four front teeth.
As per P.W.2, the petitioner has suffered disability of 45%.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the petitioner was treated conservatively and the fracture sustained by her are united.
Further it is pertinent to note that, no where in the evidence the P.W.2 has stated that, the petitioner requires any further treatment or with regard to the future medical expenses.
There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any medical treatment in future with respect to injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Nil 2.
Medical expenses 1,51,407-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 4,000-00 5.
Food and nourishment 4,000-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 2,73,407-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,73,407/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-EA-8664 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Sowjanya vs Nishanth Vijaya Varsiya on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161046484/
9 petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,73,407/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,73,407/- (Rupees two lakh seventy three thousand four hundred and seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No.
KA-09-EA-8664 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664 in the alleged accident.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further, the petitioner/ P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to her self rash and negligent driving and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending motorcycle bearing No. KA-09-EA-8664.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and the accident has taken place on account of dashing the offending motorcycle to the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and there was no negligence on the part of petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.4, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-EA-8664.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, there is no fault or negligence on the part of rider of Sowjanya vs Nishanth Vijaya Varsiya on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161046484/
5 offending motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
The petitioner has not produced any document to show that, due to accidental injuries she has suffered any physical disability.
The oral and documentary evidence on record clearly goes to show that, the petitioner has not suffered any physical disability and the injuries suffered by her are completely cured.
Further, the petitioner has failed to establish that, before accident she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of future income.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was doing Field Executive Loan Collector work and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore,
notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2021.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any medical treatment in future with respect to injuries sustained in the accident.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.

21. ISSUE No.3:

ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,73,407/- (Rupees two lakh seventy three thousand four hundred and seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.

Draw award accordingly.
